sections.h2: Where is the Berrien County Register of Deeds, and what are its hours?
sections.html:
The office occupies the Berrien County Administration Center, 701 Main Street, St. Joseph, MI 49085. Staff work weekdays except county holidays, from 8:30 in the morning until 5 in the afternoon. Documents are accepted for recording only between 8:30 and 4:30, and the public search terminals shut off at 4:45.

Questions go to 269-983-7111, extension 8562. Berrien sits in the far southwest corner of the state. The county's own list shows 8 cities, 9 villages and 22 townships, so deeds reach this counter from Benton Harbor, New Buffalo, Niles, Three Oaks and many places between.

  • Deliver the original in person, by courier, or by USPS, UPS or FedEx to 701 Main Street.
  • Add a stamped envelope with your own address so the recorded paper finds its way back to the right party.
  • Only an original bearing original signatures can be recorded, and copies are turned away.
  • Full payment is due when the paper is submitted. The office takes checks made to the Register of Deeds and cannot handle checks meant for other county departments.

sections.h2: What are the recording charges in Berrien County?
sections.html:
The county's fee page quotes $30 to record a document of any length, and its FAQ calls that Michigan's flat fee for each recordable event. A deed may also draw a tax certification charge and transfer tax on top.

Berrien County recording office charges. Source: Berrien County Register of Deeds fee page.
ItemCharge
Record one document, any number of pages$30
Every added instrument assigned or discharged$3
Tax certification covering up to 25 parcel descriptions$5
Each further parcel description20 cents
Copy of a record$1 a page
Copy on paper bigger than tabloid size$3 a page
Certified copy of a recorded document$5 plus $1 a page
Search of the indexes50 cents per year, $5 minimum

A certificate from the treasurer is required with warranty deeds, deeds that carry a warranty covenant, land contracts and their assignments, and condominium master deeds.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax does a Berrien County seller owe?
sections.html:
For a deed worth $100 or more that is not exempt, Berrien lists a county tax of 55 cents per $500 of value and a state tax of $3.75 per $500, with any leftover fraction treated as a full $500. The two together come to $4.30 per $500. A transfer tax rate chart on the county site converts sale prices to dollar figures.

The whole price must appear on the deed, or a real estate valuation affidavit goes with it. A claimed exemption belongs on the instrument itself.

Work an example with the Census median owner occupied home value of $224,300. That price holds 449 blocks of $500 after rounding up. State tax is 449 times $3.75, or $1,683.75, and county tax is 449 times 55 cents, or $246.95. The total collected at recording is $1,930.70. Your sales contract decides who pays it, so check with the title agent.

Exemptions vary by statute. The state act, MCL 207.526, excuses deeds from a parent to a child, from a grandparent to a grandchild, court orders that set no price, and transfers made in a mortgage foreclosure. The county act, MCL 207.505, covers many similar cases but does not list family transfers, so confirm which tax applies before you sign.

sections.h2: What does the Berrien County office require before it will record a document?
sections.html:
The county keeps a recording requirements page and answers common questions in its FAQ. These points arise often with sellers and with estates.

  • A death certificate must be a certified copy carrying the clerk's seal. Under MCL 565.48 you bring it to record the death of a joint owner. The earlier deed remains the latest deed of record until a new one is filed.
  • Court documents need the court's certification and seal.
  • For a notary, try the County Clerk by appointment on the main number, extension 8233, or a bank, municipal office or title company, some of which charge a fee.
  • Staff will not draft your deed. The county suggests an attorney or title insurer and mentions that templates exist online and at office supply stores.
  • Mortgage survey reports do not go on file here. Only a certified survey that was actually recorded appears in the index.

Anything recorded becomes a public record that anyone may copy for $1 a page. When a loan is paid off, the lender records a discharge of mortgage here, and the buyer's closer will look for it.

sections.h2: How do I search land records or use eRecording in Berrien County?
sections.html:
The county site has a Land Records Search page for lookups and a separate e-Recording page for electronic filing. A property and taxes page also links Register of Deeds online services, the transfer tax rate chart, and a flowchart explaining how to split or combine a parcel.

Before closing, run a name search to see the chain of title, open mortgages and any recorded liens. The statutory search charge at the counter is 50 cents per year searched. A seller who plans to keep part of a lot should read the county's split and combine flowchart first, because that process involves other offices and not this one.

Anyone selling a home that was inherited should pull the earlier deed and any recorded death certificate before listing, so the title agent can see exactly who holds the interest.

sections.h2: How do Berrien County housing figures compare for sellers?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts estimates 152,444 residents for July 2025, down 1.3 percent from the 2020 base, over 567.78 square miles of land. The county has 78,132 housing units and 63,999 households, and 72.8 percent of occupied homes are lived in by their owners.

From 2020 to 2024 the median home value was $224,300 and the median household income was $65,425. Owners with a mortgage paid a median $1,462 a month, and median gross rent was $942. About 7.9 percent of residents speak a language other than English at home, a number that can matter for interpreter and notary needs at a closing. Builders took out 372 permits in 2025.

Compared with Bay County, with a median value of $152,200, and Benzie County, at $285,700, Berrien sits between the two, so transfer tax runs higher than in Bay and lower than in Benzie for a median priced sale.

faqs.q: What does Berrien County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: A flat $30 per recordable document, whatever its page count. One paper that assigns or discharges several instruments adds $3 for each extra instrument.

faqs.q: What transfer tax rates does Berrien County post?
faqs.a: County tax is 55 cents per $500 of value and state tax is $3.75 per $500, each counted by $500 or fraction. Together that is $4.30 per $500, unless the deed is exempt.

faqs.q: Can I send a deed to Berrien County by mail?
faqs.a: Yes. Mail the original, with original signatures, to 701 Main Street, St. Joseph, MI 49085, with full payment and a stamped return envelope. Photocopies cannot be recorded.

faqs.q: Until what time does Berrien County record documents?
faqs.a: Recording ends at 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, although the office stays open until 5:00 p.m. and public search terminals close at 4:45 p.m.

faqs.q: Can the Berrien County Register of Deeds notarize my deed?
faqs.a: No. Notaries work in the County Clerk's office, reached at 269-983-7111, extension 8233, and in banks, municipal offices and title companies, some of which charge for it.
